subject: Private deployment: keystore escrow, subprocessor notice, and geo-routing options

Subject: Private deployment — keystore escrow & subproc notice

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. We are moving toward procurement but need to close a few privacy/security items for our Private deployment (VPC / on-prem). High level asks from security and procurement:

- BYOK escrow: procurement will only sign if we have an escrow model that prevents operator access except under emergency with attestation.
- Subprocessor notice & approvals: we need a standing list of subprocessors and 30-day notice before any new subprocessor is enabled; some data planes may not permit offshoring.
- Telemetry & routing: all telemetry and health pings must remain in the EU for HelioMed unless otherwise authorized; we need proof of routing.
- Evidence & audits: SOC2 excerpts or audit evidence for operator breakglass events and retention of logs for 12 months.

Can you confirm Redwood's recommended approach and share any standard language you propose for the DPA/addendum? Procurement also requests an initial redline so they can share with legal.

Attaching a one-pager from our legal team describing the BYOK constraints.

Regards,
James Lee
Sr. Security PM | HelioMed

Attachment: helio_byo_requirements.pdf (attachment stub)

Subject: Re: Private deployment — keystore escrow & subproc notice

James — thanks, and really appreciate the clarity.

Short answer: we can support two deployment patterns that map to the asks you listed, and I'll summarize both below. I've copied Kim (legal) and Karthik (solutions) to propose specific contract language and technical constraints.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call tomorrow to run through the options and identify which path HelioMed prefers before procurement sends formal redlines. I attached our procurement checklist and a starter BYOK escrow clause (PDF) — Kim will note changes.

Option A (managed private):
- Redwood hosts control plane in customer-dedicated VPC/region; customer supplies CMK; Redwood holds escrowed partial key material in an HSM escrow split.
- Operator access to full keystore requires breakglass + double-signed attestation + access recorded in audit trail.
- Telemetry defaults to EU-only routing for this account.
- Standard subprocessor notice with 30-day window, with an SLT for critical subprocessors to require customer approval.

Option B (customer-keystore):
- HelioMed retains full keystore (no escrow). Redwood provides deploy-runbook and on-prem installation support under an MSA.
- This reduces operator risk but increases procurement time and requires an elevated support contract.

I can host the call and propose a mutual action plan. Proposed times: Tue 22 Jun 14:00 UTC or Wed 23 Jun 09:00 UTC.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 1212

Attachments: procurement_checklist.xlsx; redline_byok_escrow_draft.pdf

James/Ben —

I've reviewed Ben's starter escrow clause and HelioMed's requirements. High-level legal points and suggested redlines below (see attached PDF for inline redline):

1) Subprocessors: we will provide a current list at contract signature and add a contract clause requiring 30-calendar-day notice before onboarding a new subprocessor that will process customer data for private deployments. For subprocessors that perform critical control-plane functions, we propose an approval carve-out (i.e., customer approval required).

2) Escrow/Breakglass: propose split-escrow with the customer retaining half of the key material (or a passphrase) and Redwood holding the other half. Operator access requires: (a) documented emergency, (b) two Redwood approvers + customer affirmation (email), and (c) a signed attestation posted in our audit logs. Limit operator access to a set of named engineers and require per-access ticketing and post-incident root-cause.

3) Geo-routing & Telemetry: add a contractual commitment that operational telemetry for the HelioMed tenancy will be routed through EU-based telemetry collectors and stored in the EU unless the customer explicitly authorizes otherwise. Telemetry categories must be enumerated (health pings, aggregated performance metrics, operator logs) and sensitive traces excluded by default.

4) Evidence & Audit: we can provide SOC2 reports and a targeted evidence package for breakglass events on a reasonable frequency (quarterly or on-demand for major incidents). For the procurement redline, we can offer 12-month retention of operator breakglass logs (encrypted at rest) and a process for forensic evidence export.

5) Export Controls / Cross-border: clause to restrict cross-border transfers of customer data and key material except as required by law or mutually agreed exception.

I'll attach a redline PDF with exact language. If HelioMed wants the stronger Option B (no escrow, customer-keystore), procurement should expect a longer onboarding schedule and an elevated professional services SOW for on-prem install & periodic evidence collection.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_byok_escrow_draft.pdf

Team / James —

Technical clarifications and operational constraints to align with Kim's legal proposals:

- Escrow model: recommend an HSM-backed split-escrow where each share is sealed. In Option A we can automate key reconstruction only after an automated checklist + custodian approval webflow that requires an inbound signed confirmation from the customer's security mailbox. This keeps an auditable trail and minimizes manual operator handling.

- Operator access minimization: implement short-lived operator sessions (EPHEMERAL KMS token) and require recorded session replay. We can restrict operator roles to named RBAC groups tied to incident tickets.

- Telemetry routing: to guarantee EU-only routing we will provision dedicated telemetry collectors in eu-west-1 and block routing rules for other regions for the HelioMed tenant. That has a small infra lead time (3–5 business days) and requires inclusion in the deployment manifest.

- Subprocessors: we will enumerate subsystem-level subprocessors (monitoring, patch management, CDNs). For any subprocessor that handles key material reconstruction we will mark them as "critical" and add the approval carve-out in the DPA.

- Automation & SOW: Option B (customer-keystore) will need an on-prem SOW that includes a handover checklist, runbook updates, and quarterly evidence exports. Estimate for full on-prem rollout: 6–8 weeks (PS + infra prep).

Link to the telemetry routing notes: https://drive.redwood.company/drive/folders/11aByoK-Helio-Docs

Happy to review on the call.

—Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

Thanks again for the clear asks. To keep procurement moving, below are two clean options and the immediate asks from Redwood to enable contracting: please reply with which option you prefer (A or B) and confirm availability for a 30-minute call.

Option A — Managed Private (recommended for faster onboarding)
- BYOK with split-escrow (Redwood holds part; HelioMed retains part).
- Operator breakglass only with customer affirmation + double approval; full audit trail retained for 12 months.
- Telemetry & ops routing: EU-only by default.
- Subprocessors: 30-day notice; approval required for "critical" subprocessors.
- Estimated onboarding: 2–3 weeks from contract signature.

Option B — Customer-keystore (recommended for maximum control)
- HelioMed retains keys; Redwood provides install SOW and runbook support.
- No escrow, operator access is not possible by design.
- Higher PS cost; estimated onboarding: 6–8 weeks.

Immediate asks from Redwood to produce redlines:
1) Confirm option selection (A or B).
2) Provide any mandatory legal text from HelioMed that must be included (export control clauses, minimum insurance wording, etc.).
3) Confirm contact for technical validation and the security mailbox we should require for breakglass confirmations.
